claim: The report of the Boston committee says that on visiting parts of the battle-field and hospital burying-yards they found that the bodies of rebel soldiers were generally buried in trenches, in numbers from five to one hundred, and Union soldiers invariably in separate graves.

source.edition: Report of the Joint Special Committee on the burial of Massachusetts dead at Gettysburg (Boston, 1863)

quote: Upon visiting some parts of the battle-field and hospital burying-yards, they found that as a general thing the bodies of rebel soldiers were buried in trenches, in numbers varying from five to one hundred. Union soldiers, on the contrary, were invariably buried in separate graves

data.practice: rebel dead in trenches of five to one hundred; Union dead in separate graves
data.place: the battle-field and the hospital burying-yards

scene.may_show: Trench graves holding five to one hundred Confederate dead and rows of separate Union graves, with headboards, on the field and in the hospital burying-yards.
scene.reduced_form: rows of simple grave mounds with headboards

notes: the OCR has no reliable page marker here (printed page 9 or 10); the date of the visit is before 1 October 1863, not printed in the sentence

claim: The Boston committee reports that the effluvia arising from the decay of hundreds of unburied horses, with the impure state of the air, made the labor of finding the graves peculiarly unpleasant.

source.edition: Report of the Joint Special Committee on the burial of Massachusetts dead at Gettysburg (Boston, 1863)

quote: The effluvia arising from the decay of hundreds of unburied horses, together with the impure state of the air incident to the time and place, rendered the labor peculiarly unpleasant.

data.practice: hundreds of horses lay unburied when the committee searched for the graves

scene.may_show: Unburied horse carcasses lying about the field while men search for graves; the air is foul.
scene.reduced_form: shapes of dead horses at a distance

claim: The letter at the head of the Boston committee's report says that a large proportion of those who fell were buried by their surviving comrades on the field of battle and received only such hasty rites of sepulture as the circumstances would warrant.

source.edition: Report of the Joint Special Committee on the burial of Massachusetts dead at Gettysburg (Boston, 1863)

quote: A large proportion of them were buried by their surviving comrades on the field of battle, but received only such hasty rites of sepulture as the circumstances would warrant.

data.practice: buried by surviving comrades on the field with hasty rites
